articles.title: Trade unions in India say they should participate in determining minimum wage
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Workers and leaders of the major trade unions in India came out to protest against the government’s decision to keep them out of the newly constructed Central Minimum Wage Advisory Board on Monday, September 7. The protest was called by the left-wing Center for Indian Trade Unions (CITU), the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC), and the centrist Indian National Trade Union Congress (INTUC), for demanding proper representation in decisions related to salaries. The three are among India’s largest trade union federations with millions of members each, with AITUC being the oldest in the country. articles.title: Confronting the ecological crisis
articles.author: Paul Fleckenstein
articles.content_excerpt: T he ecological crisis is upon us. It touches everywhere on the planet. Its character is complex, manifesting in floods, fires, disease, eradication of forests and fisheries. Interacting factors worsen globally connected catastrophes. Ian Angus’s Metabolic Rifts: Capitalism Assault on the Earth System makes an important contribution to understanding and guiding a socialist response to these compounding ecological crises. Angus is an ecological Marxist scholar and founding member of the Global Ecosocialist Network . Metabolic Rifts connects modern science, history, and Marxism’s metabolic rift theory. articles.content_excerpt: Ahead of the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has unsealed more than 170,000 pages of records that offer new insights into how the city responded to the disaster. articles.title: “Let’s Just Round Them Up”: The Rise of Islamophobia in the Post-9/11 Domestic War on Terror
articles.content_excerpt: The attacks on September 11, 2001, unleashed a wave of Islamophobia in the United States that resulted in widespread harassment and persecution of Muslim Americans. In addition to vigilante attacks targeting Muslims or those perceived to be Muslim, there was also state repression including police roundups, community surveillance, prosecutions on often flimsy terrorism charges and mass deportations. articles.title: US votes against UN resolution promoting maps reflecting Africa’s true size
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: The United Nations General Assembly has backed an African-led initiative calling for a more accurate representation of the world’s continents, particularly Africa, in maps used in education, public communication, and other areas. articles.title: Croatians demand their government stop importing toxic waste
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: On Saturday, September 5, around 100,000 people took to the streets of Zagreb to protest against illegal toxic waste disposal in the Lika region. The mobilization, one of the most notable in recent years, brought together diverse networks from all over Croatia. Protesters demanded not only the clearing of the affected areas in Gospić, but also accountability from the government and a pledge to temporarily halt waste imports into the country. This final demand relates to the fact that tens of thousands of tons of illegal waste found at several dumping sites across the country originated from Slovenia, Italy, and Germany.
